text: The pipeline begins by constructing an image graph and evaluating depth reliability.
First, the framework takes the input RGB image.
It decomposes the RGB image into superpixels via SLIC segmentation to form the graph nodes.
In parallel, the corresponding depth image is received.
By analyzing the depth statistical distribution, the model computes a depth confidence measure to mitigate the influence of noisy depth maps.
The graph representation and confidence measure are forwarded to a two-stage saliency computation framework.
In Stage one, compactness saliency is calculated by evaluating spatial spread using both color and depth cues.
Next, a depth-refined foreground seed selection mechanism identifies reliable salient seeds.
In Stage two, foreground saliency is computed by measuring contrast against these seeds across color, depth, and texture cues.
The compactness and foreground saliency maps are fused together through a weighted sum.
Finally, the integrated saliency map is generated, accurately highlighting the salient object in comparison with the ground truth.
